column3: Hebrew has a singular “evil man” and “man of violence”; BSB uses plurals.
Hebrew has a singular “heart” and plural “wars”; BSB has “hearts” and singular “war.”
Hebrew has singular “tongue,” “snake,” and “adder,” and puts the poison “under” their lips; BSB uses plurals and “on.”
Hebrew has a singular “man of violence” and says they plot to thrust down “my steps”; BSB has plural men and “make me stumble.”
Hebrew keeps the proud as active subjects spreading the net and setting traps; BSB uses passive clauses for both actions.
Hebrew says “I said”; BSB has “I say.”
Hebrew describes covering the head as completed and says “day of weaponry”; BSB has present “shield” and “day of battle.”
Hebrew has singular “his plan,” not “their evil plans,” and active “they will rise,” rather than passive “they be exalted.”
Hebrew has singular “head” and says the trouble of their lips covers “them”; BSB makes plural heads the subject of being covered.
Hebrew uses an active singular verb, “he will throw them”; BSB uses passive “they be thrown.” “Miry” is not explicit before “pits.”
Hebrew calls the slanderer a “man of tongue” and ends with “for overthrows”; BSB leaves the latter phrase unexpressed.
Hebrew has one future action, doing the poor man’s cause and the needy’s justice; BSB uses present “upholds” and “defends.”
Hebrew says the righteous “give thanks” to His name; BSB says “praise.” It retains the image of dwelling with His face.
